title: Linear thresholds have degree at most one
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$. If there are real weights $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ and a real constant $a_0$ such that $f(x)$ is the sign of $a_0+\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i$ for every $x$, with zero assigned the positive sign, then $f$ is represented by the sign of a real-valued polynomial on the cube whose Fourier degree is at most $1$.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean function on the n-dimensional sign cube
Existence of real weights and constant giving a linear threshold representation
